title: Section check: Evidence and early connections
intro: 6 questions about Lessons 1–3. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.

questions.question: You look at the photo of the Ban Chiang pot. You say, "It has painted swirls." Which word fits what you said?

options.text: An inference, an idea to test
options.feedback: Not quite. An inference is an idea that explains what you see. You can see the swirls, so this is an observation. Look back at Lesson 1.

options.text: An observation, a thing you see
options.feedback: Yes. The swirls are there in the photo. You can see them, so this is an observation.

options.text: Context, where the pot was found
options.feedback: Not quite. Context is where a find lay in the ground and what was near it. The photo does not show that. Look back at Lesson 1.

stimulus.title: A made-up find from a made-up dig
stimulus.body: This is a made-up example. At the made-up site of Vessa, a team digs up a clay bowl with painted lines. It lay in a grave, next to a bronze ring. A student writes, "The owner of this bowl was a farmer."

questions.question: What does the student need before they can say this?

options.text: More evidence than the bowl alone
options.feedback: Yes. A bowl cannot tell us what its owner did. Other finds and records might help, and the answer may stay unsure.

options.text: Nothing, as the painted lines prove it
options.feedback: Not quite. The lines show that someone painted the bowl. They do not show what its owner did. Look back at Lesson 1.

options.text: A clearer photo of the painted lines
options.feedback: Not quite. A clearer photo still shows only the bowl. It cannot show who owned it. Look back at Lesson 1.

questions.question: Look at the 2015 photo of the balangay planks. Which claim does it support?

options.text: The boat sailed from Butuan to China
options.feedback: Not quite. The photo shows planks, not a route. It cannot show where the boat went. Look back at Lesson 2.
Not quite. Nobody found the pottery inside a boat. The pottery is a different find. Look back at Lesson 2.

options.text: People in Butuan built plank boats
options.feedback: Yes. You can see the wooden planks and the holes along them. They show how people built boats.

questions.question: On the lesson's map, the lines from Butuan to other places are dashed. Why?

options.text: They show links that were possible
options.feedback: Yes. The boats and the imported pottery are clues to links by sea. But no source shows one exact trip.

options.text: They show the exact route of one boat
options.feedback: Not quite. No source tells us where the Butuan boats sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.

options.text: They show trips that boats made each year
options.feedback: Not quite. The sources do not say how often anyone sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.

questions.question: The map of Melaka is dated 1604. Which time can it help you study?

options.text: Melaka in the 1400s, under the sultanate
options.feedback: Not quite. The sultanate came first, in the 1400s. The map was made about 90 years after the Portuguese took the city. Look back at Lesson 3.

options.text: Melaka in the time of Portuguese rule
options.feedback: Yes. The Portuguese took Melaka in 1511, and the map comes from their time. It cannot show the city of the 1400s.

options.text: Melaka today, as a heritage city
options.feedback: Not quite. The map is more than 400 years old. UNESCO's modern record tells us about Melaka today. Look back at Lesson 3.

questions.question: The 1604 map shows a big fort, a river and roads. Whose view is hard to find on it?

options.feedback: Not quite. The map shows what the mapmaker chose to draw. It shows his perspective. Look back at Lesson 3.
Not quite. UNESCO wrote about Melaka in modern times. That is a different source from the map. Look back at Lesson 3.
Yes. The map shows a fort and roads, but few homes or people at work. Their view is hard to find.

results.high: Well done. You can tell what an object or a map shows from what we guess about it.
results.middle: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.low: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 1–3, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
